title: Dos and Don’ts / red UI elements
slide_intent: Choose a functional red deliberately so a recognizable accent remains readable in controls.
strategic_value: A darker red for interface elements can support DB’s accessibility intentions without abandoning its color cue.
demonstration: A button in DB Red 500 is paired with a crossed-out brighter DB Red button.
practical_value: Select DB Red 500 for the red interface element shown.

content_islands.name: UI-red comparison
content_islands.spec: Place the accepted darker red button left and the crossed-out brighter version right with their accessibility captions.

reference_purposes.Intent: The captions explicitly ground the darker-red choice in accessibility.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Red UI elements use DB Red 500 rather than the brighter DB Red.

ingredient.name: Red interface controls
ingredient.role: Preserve recognizable emphasis with the specified functional contrast.
ingredient.application: Use DB Red 500 for red UI elements.
ingredient.scope: This rule concerns interface elements; identity specimens such as the DB mark use the separate brand-red guidance.
